{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py",
      "line": 11,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now an abstract class and cannot be instantiated",
      "body": "MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but does not implement the abstract members required by that class (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data). Since MetricAlertFire.detector_handler points to this class, Detector.detector_handler will raise TypeError when it attempts to instantiate the handler for a metric_alert_fire detector. Previously this handler was concrete and safely returned an empty evaluation result."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py",
      "line": 222,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "get_state_data raises KeyError for stateful handlers with no counters",
      "body": "In StatefulDetectorHandler.get_state_data, if self.counter_names is empty, counter_updates remains an empty dict, but the code later unconditionally accesses counter_updates[gk] for each group key. A valid StatefulDetectorHandler subclass with counter_names == [] will therefore crash during evaluation. The method should initialize counter_updates as {gk: {} for gk in group_keys} or use counter_updates.get(gk, {})."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py",
      "line": 326,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Redis keys collide for group_key None and empty string",
      "body": "build_dedupe_value_key converts a None group_key to an empty string before formatting, and build_counter_value_key does the same. This makes a None group key and an empty-string group key produce identical Redis keys for dedupe values and counters. If an empty string can be returned by get_group_key_values, state for one group key can overwrite or block the other, causing incorrect deduplication or wrong alert state. Use an unambiguous sentinel/encoding for None instead of collapsing it to ''."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py",
      "line": 62,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Occurrences are produced before detector state is committed",
      "body": "process_detectors calls create_issue_occurrence_from_result for each evaluation result before handler.commit_state_updates is called. If the process crashes or the state commit fails after the Kafka produce call, the dedupe/state used to prevent reprocessing is not persisted. A retry or reprocessing of the same data packet can then pass the dedupe check again and emit duplicate occurrences or status changes."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py",
      "line": 159,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "get_group_key_values return annotation excludes supported None group keys",
      "body": "StatefulDetectorHandler.get_group_key_values is annotated as returning dict[str, int], but DetectorGroupKey is used throughout this module and None is explicitly supported (for example in bulk_get_detector_state, Redis key builders, and tests). Subclasses that return {None: value} will fail type checking. The return type should be dict[DetectorGroupKey, int]."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py",
      "line": 230,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "doc_defect",
      "title": "StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate docstring still says it returns a list",
      "body": "The docstring for StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, but the method now returns dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]. This is misleading for implementers and callers after the signature change."
    },
    {
      "file": "tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py",
      "line": 191,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "Multi-group test builds the second expected occurrence with the wrong value",
      "body": "In test_state_results_multi_group, the data packet contains {'group_1': 6, 'group_2': 10}, but the expected occurrence for group_2 is built with value 6 instead of 10. The current mock occurrence builder ignores value, so the test passes without verifying that the hook receives the correct value for each group key."
    }

findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now an abstract class and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but does not implement the abstract members required by that class (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data). Since MetricAlertFire.detector_handler points to this class, Detector.detector_handler will raise TypeError when it attempts to instantiate the handler for a metric_alert_fire detector. Previously this handler was concrete and safely returned an empty evaluation result.

findings.title: get_state_data raises KeyError for stateful handlers with no counters
findings.body: In StatefulDetectorHandler.get_state_data, if self.counter_names is empty, counter_updates remains an empty dict, but the code later unconditionally accesses counter_updates[gk] for each group key. A valid StatefulDetectorHandler subclass with counter_names == [] will therefore crash during evaluation. The method should initialize counter_updates as {gk: {} for gk in group_keys} or use counter_updates.get(gk, {}).

findings.title: Redis keys collide for group_key None and empty string
findings.body: build_dedupe_value_key converts a None group_key to an empty string before formatting, and build_counter_value_key does the same. This makes a None group key and an empty-string group key produce identical Redis keys for dedupe values and counters. If an empty string can be returned by get_group_key_values, state for one group key can overwrite or block the other, causing incorrect deduplication or wrong alert state. Use an unambiguous sentinel/encoding for None instead of collapsing it to ''.

findings.title: Occurrences are produced before detector state is committed
findings.body: process_detectors calls create_issue_occurrence_from_result for each evaluation result before handler.commit_state_updates is called. If the process crashes or the state commit fails after the Kafka produce call, the dedupe/state used to prevent reprocessing is not persisted. A retry or reprocessing of the same data packet can then pass the dedupe check again and emit duplicate occurrences or status changes.

findings.title: get_group_key_values return annotation excludes supported None group keys
findings.body: StatefulDetectorHandler.get_group_key_values is annotated as returning dict[str, int], but DetectorGroupKey is used throughout this module and None is explicitly supported (for example in bulk_get_detector_state, Redis key builders, and tests). Subclasses that return {None: value} will fail type checking. The return type should be dict[DetectorGroupKey, int].

findings.title: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: The docstring for StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, but the method now returns dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]. This is misleading for implementers and callers after the signature change.

findings.title: Multi-group test builds the second expected occurrence with the wrong value
findings.body: In test_state_results_multi_group, the data packet contains {'group_1': 6, 'group_2': 10}, but the expected occurrence for group_2 is built with value 6 instead of 10. The current mock occurrence builder ignores value, so the test passes without verifying that the hook receives the correct value for each group key.
